'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Somali Civil War]]
**[[2025 Shabelle offensive]]
***[[Al-Shabaab (militant group)|Al-Shabaab]] targets two military bases operated by [[AUSSOM]] and the [[Somali Armed Forces]] near the Somali capital [[Mogadishu]] using a bomb-laden attack. [https://www.garoweonline.com/en/news/somalia/al-shabaab-targets-military-bases-near-somali-capital-with-bomb-laden-assault (Garowe Online)]
**[[Jubaland crisis]]
***Following the capture of [[Beled Hawo]] by [[Jubaland]] forces, Somali federal troops are deployed to reinforce federal government presence in [[Gedo]]. [https://www.garoweonline.com/en/news/somalia/somalia-federal-troop-deployment-sparks-fears-of-renewed-conflict-in-gedo-region (Garowe Online)]
*[[War against the Islamic State]]
**[[Islamic State insurgency in Puntland]]
***In a joint [[military operation]], [[Puntland counter-terrorism operations|Puntland Counter-Terrorism forces]] and [[US SOF]] capture the financial and foreign recruitment chief of [[ISIS-Somalia]], Abdiweli Mohamed Aw Yusuf "Abdiweli Walalac," and two others. The operation took place in the Laag area of rural Xumbeys in the [[Bari Region|Bari region]] of [[Puntland]]. [https://www.garoweonline.com/en/news/somalia/somalia-puntland-forces-with-u-s-support-capture-senior-isis-leader (Garowe Online)]
**[[US intervention in the Syrian civil war]]
***[[United States Central Command|U.S. Central Command]] kills senior [[Islamic State]] leader Diaa Zoubaa Musleh Al-Hardani along with his two sons in a strike on [[Al-Bab]], [[Aleppo Governorate]], [[Syria]]. [https://english.alarabiya.net/News/middle-east/2025/07/25/us-centcom-says-it-killed-senior-isis-leader-in-syria (Al Arabiya)]
*[[2025 Cambodia–Thailand border conflict]]
**[[2025 Cambodia–Thailand clashes]]
***The [[Royal Thai Armed Forces]]'s Border Defense Command declares [[martial law]] in eight districts of the provinces of [[Chanthaburi province|Chanthaburi]] and [[Trat province|Trat]] on [[Cambodia–Thailand border|their border with Cambodia]], citing "Cambodia's use of force to enter Thai territory". [https://www.ndtv.com/world-news/thailand-declares-martial-law-in-8-districts-bordering-cambodia-after-deadly-clashes-news-agency-afp-8949722 (NDTV)]
***The [[Royal Thai Air Force]] launches [[airstrike]]s on targets inside [[Cambodia]], including areas near the [[Preah Vihear Temple]] and [[Prasat Ta Muen Thom]]. [https://www.nationthailand.com/news/asean/40053066 (''Nation Thailand'')] [https://www.thestar.com.my/aseanplus/aseanplus-news/2025/07/25/thai-air-force-deploys-f-16s-to-bomb-cambodian-targets-in-three-key-strategic-areas (''The Star'')]
*[[Kivu conflict]]
**[[M23 campaign (2022–present)|M23 campaign]]
***[[Wazalendo]] fighters launch an offensive to take the town of Luke, [[Masisi Territory]], [[Democratic Republic of the Congo]], which the [[March 23 Movement]] had taken the previous day. [https://www.radiookapi.net/2025/07/25/actualite/securite/nord-kivu-violents-affrontements-entre-m23-et-groupes-armes-locaux (Radio Okapi)]
***The [[Alliance of Patriots for a Free and Sovereign Congo]] of the Wazalendo resist an attack on their positions by the M23 in the area of Showa, Masisi Territory. Residents of Luke, Showa, and Bukombo flee to escape the fighting. [https://www.radiookapi.net/2025/07/25/actualite/securite/nord-kivu-violents-affrontements-entre-m23-et-groupes-armes-locaux (Radio Okapi)]
*[[Russian invasion of Ukraine]]
**[[Pokrovsk offensive]], [[Kupiansk offensive]]
***[[Russian Armed Forces|Russian forces]] enter the city of [[Pokrovsk]] for the first time since the invasion began, and enter the city of [[Kupiansk]] for the first time since 2024. [https://www.understandingwar.org/backgrounder/russian-offensive-campaign-assessment-july-25-2025 (ISW)]
*[[Ituri conflict]]
**Two [[Mai-Mai]] militias continue to fight over the control of agricultural roads in Babila-Babombi chiefdom, [[Mambasa Territory]], DRC. Residents of several villages flee to escape the fighting. [https://www.radiookapi.net/2025/07/25/actualite/securite/ituri-affrontements-entre-factions-mai-mai-mambasa-des-milliers-de (Radio Okapi)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[Piplodi school roof collapse]]
**A school collapse caused by continuous rainfall in [[Piplodi]], [[Jhalawar District]], [[India]], kills at least seven students, seriously injures 28 others, including eight critically, and traps over 32 under debris. [https://indianexpress.com/article/india/rajasthan-school-building-collapse-jhalawar-children-trapped-toll-rescue-ops-10148248/ (''The Indian Express'')]
*[[Mediterranean Sea migrant smuggling]]
**A boat carrying [[Egypt]]ian migrants and [[Sudan]]ese crewmen en route to Europe capsizes off the coast of [[Tobruk]], [[Cyrenaica]], [[Libya]], killing at least 15 people, injuring 10 others and leaving some missing. [https://apnews.com/article/migrants-libya-boat-egyptians-europe-boat-coast-sea-3d0a471e7fde93dadc1706fdc3c09ce3 (AP)]
*A gas explosion at a ten-story apartment building in [[Saratov]], [[Saratov Oblast]], Russia kills at least six people, including a child, injures seven others and destroys or damages over 30 apartments. [https://www.aa.com.tr/en/asia-pacific/5-killed-7-injured-in-gas-explosion-in-russias-city-of-saratov/3642086 (Anadolu Agency)] [https://novayagazeta.eu/articles/2025/07/25/four-dead-as-block-of-flats-in-russian-city-of-saratov-partially-collapses-after-suspected-gas-explosion-en-news (Novaya Gazeta)]

'''International relations'''
*[[India–Maldives relations]]
**[[India]]n [[Prime Minister of India|prime minister]] [[Narendra Modi]] announces India will lend a US$565 million [[line of credit|credit line]] to the [[Maldives]], gift their [[Maldives National Defence Force|armed forces]] several [[Infantry fighting vehicles|heavy fighting vehicles]], and launch formal talks for a [[free-trade agreement]]. [https://apnews.com/article/india-maldives-modi-muizzu-credit-independence-ad1834dc3f26e74890b25d743639f177 (AP)]
*[[Palau–United States relations]]
**The [[traditional chiefs of Palau]] and the [[Palau National Congress|National Congress]] reject a proposal by the [[United States]] to host asylum seekers and strongly advise [[President of Palau|President]] [[Surangel Whipps Jr.]] to also reject it. [https://islandtimes.org/palau-leaders-reject-u-s-proposal-to-host-asylum-seekers/ (''Island Times'')]

'''Law and crime'''
*The trial of former [[Democratic Republic of the Congo|Congolese]] [[President of the Democratic Republic of the Congo|president]] and [[senator for life]] [[Joseph Kabila]] for his crimes in connection with the [[March 23 Movement|M23 Movement]] and the [[Congo River Alliance]] begins. The [[Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of the Congo|armed forces]] auditor general charges Kabila with [[treason]], participation in an [[insurrection]]al movement, crimes against the peace and security of humanity, intentional homicide, rape, torture, deportation, and condoning crimes. [https://www.radiookapi.net/2025/07/25/actualite/justice/rdc-ouverture-du-proces-de-joseph-kabila-ce-vendredi-devant-la-haute (Radio Okapi)]
*The [[Government of Hong Kong|government]] of [[Hong Kong]] places a [[Hong Kong dollar|HK$]]200,000 (US$25,500) bounty on 19 members of the overseas [[Pro-democracy camp (Hong Kong)|pro-democracy]] organization [[Hong Kong Parliament Electoral Organizing Committee|Hong Kong Parliament]]. [https://www.dw.com/en/hong-kong-places-bounty-on-19-pro-democracy-activists/a-73407151 (DW)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[First impeachment of Sara Duterte|Impeachment of Sara Duterte]]
**The [[Supreme Court of the Philippines]] rules that the [[Impeachment in the Philippines|impeachment]] complaint against [[Vice President of the Philippines|Vice President]] [[Sara Duterte]], filed by [[House of Representatives of the Philippines|the lower house of Congress]] in February, is [[Constitution of the Philippines|unconstitutional]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/philippine-supreme-court-voids-impeachment-complaint-against-vp-duterte-2025-07-25/ (Reuters)]

'''Science and technology'''
*[[Online Safety Act 2023]]
**Thousands of websites, such as [[Facebook]] and [[YouTube]], begin implementing age verification to block "adult content" for [[United Kingdom|British]] viewers under the age of 18, according to [[Ofcom]]. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c24v4dl5r16o (BBC News)] [https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2025/jul/24/what-are-the-new-uk-online-safety-rules-and-how-will-they-be-enforced (The Guardian)]
